script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for September 21. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You started as a single cell, yet that cell knew how to become you—every organ, every protein, every detail.  How?  DNA.

DNA has only four letters: A, T, C, G. Yet their combinations encode every living thing. Simple rules, combined creatively, produce infinite complexity. Constraint enables rather than limits. DNA doesn't store a miniature human—it stores instructions for building one.  The recipe, not the dish.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Instructions persist better than artifacts.  Pass on the recipe, not just the dish.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Code Audit - What Instructions Run You?.

Here's your activity: What 'code' runs your life—beliefs, assumptions, habits, values? Which did you inherit versus consciously choose? Understanding your programming is the first step to debugging or upgrading it. This helps you identify inherited and chosen operating instructions.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about the code of life can be applied to code audit - what instructions run you?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
